args.summary: Deploy v2.3.1 to production caused checkout-api to fail health checks in all regions. Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback verified: service is healthy on v2.3.0 with a 0.2% error rate. Root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation; v2.3.1 was previously unhealthy in staging (rc) as well.
args.title: checkout-api health check failures following v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Checked release history** — confirmed v2.3.1 (the latest production deploy) was unhealthy, and identified **v2.3.0** as the most recent release that was healthy in production.
2. **Rolled back** checkout-api to **v2.3.0 in all production regions** (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rollout verified.
3. **Confirmed recovery** — service is now healthy on v2.3.0 with a 0.2% error rate.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** documenting the health-check failures on v2.3.1 and the rollback; the on-call engineer has been paged.

Note for follow-up: v2.3.1 was already unhealthy in staging as a release candidate, so that deploy likely went out without staging validation — worth investigating in the incident postmortem.
